allocations.requirement_text: The PCA pump should be able to operate within a temperature range of Tlo = 10C to Thi = 50C.
The pump should be able to withstand and operate under atmospheric pressure ranging from Pmin = 20”Hg to Pmax = 35”Hg.
The (external) pump should be able to operate at relative humidity ranging from Hmin = 0% to Hmax = 100% (non-condensing).
The PCA pump shall withstand splashing (but not immersion) with water or bodily fluids.

All filled prescriptions (liquid, narcotic pain-killer dispensed by the hospital pharmacy) must be labeled at least visibly with a. Patient name b. Drug code c. Name of drug d. Concentration e. Initial volume of drug f. Basal flow rate g. VTBI h. Minimum time between bolus i. Date prescription filled j. Prescribing physician’s name k. Pharmacist name
The PCA pump shall be cleaned and disinfected after use.
The PCA pump must not leak current greater than 10 mA.
Component failure must not harm patient (beyond stopping function).

The PCA pump must be electromagnetically compatible according to IEC 60601-1-2 (2001) Medical Electrical Equipment, Part 1: General Requirements for Safety, 2. Collateral Standard: Electromagnetic Compatibility - Requirements and Tests . (IEC 60601-1-2 2.3.1)
The PCA pump must withstand electrostatic discharge.
The PCA pump must filter power interference from mains.
The PCA pump shallissue alarms and warnings that require clinician attention.
The ICE Interface shall transmit current operating status and infusion rate to the ICE system.
The ICE interface shall transmit events, alarms, and warnings to the ICE system.
The ICE interface shall allow a clinician to set the duration of clinician-requested boluses through an ICE supervisor user interface.
The PCA pump shall switch to KVO infusion rate when commanded through its ICE interface.
The PCA pump shall resume prescribed infusion when commanded through its ICE interface.
Provisioning (or re-provisioning) shall not be possible through an ICE network.
Provisioning of initial security keys which form a root of trust must require physical connection to a jack distinct from normal operation.
The provisioning jack must be physically inaccessible, except to authorized technical personnel.
The PCA pump shall detect power supply voltage out-of-range, issue a voltage out-of-range warning, and switch to battery backup when out-of-range.
The PCA pump shall detect power supply voltage out-of-range, issue a voltage out-of-range warning, and switch to battery backup when out-of-range.
The PCA pump shallissue alarms and warnings that require clinician attention.

If a visual indicator is necessary for the clinician to identify the equipment or part of the equipment that requires clinician response or awareness, at least one visual alarm signal shall be provided that: 1. indicates the priority of the highest priority alarm condition; and 2. can be perceived correctly at a distance of 4 m from the PCA pump.
The alarm indicator appearance shall comply with color, flashing frequency, and duty cycle given in Table 5.

At least one visual alarm signal shall be provided that identifies the specific alarm condition and its priority. This signal shall be perceived correctly (be legible) at a distance of 1 m from the equipment or part of the equipment or from the clinician’s position.
Visual alarms shall display alarm symbols from Table D.201 Graphical symbols for ALARM SYSTEMS of standard IEC 60601-1-8.
Alarms shall cause audible alarms signals that meet the requirements of Tables 203 and 204 of standard IEC 60601-1-8 for alarm pulses, bursts, and harmonics.
The auditory volume of audible alarms signals shall conform to Section 201.3.3.2 Volume of auditory ALARM SIGNALS and INFORMATION SIGNALS of standard IEC 60601-1-8.

The alarm melody of audible alarms signals shall conform to Table AAA.1 of standard IEC 60601-1-8 for drug or fluid delivery. “C d g” shall be used for medium priority alarms; “C d g - C d” shall be used for high priority alarms; “e c” shall be used for warnings and low priority alarms.
Each tone in the alarm melody shall be composed of a minimum of 4 harmonic components in the range 300 Hz to 4000 Hz comprising an inverted 9th jazz chord.
The control panel must display currently-programmed patient data and physician’s prescription.
The PCA pump shall have a start button.
The PCA pump shall have a stop button.
The control panel shall allow clinician bolus request and choice of duration.
A clinician must personally confirm the prescription is for the patient to be infused.
Prescriptions that violate the soft limits of the drug in the drug library shall issue a visible and audible warning requiring a soft limit confirmation by the clinician.
The Control Panel shall show alarm condition as described in Section 6.4.2.
The Control Panel shall audibly sound alarm condition as described in Section 6.4.3.
Pressing the stop button silences all alarms and terminates any alarm signal inactivation.
The Control Panel shall provide means toinactivate audible alarms indefinitely.
The Control Panel shall provide means to inactivate audible alarms temporarily for a predefined period of time.
The Control Panel shall provide means to cancel alarm signal inactivation.
When auditory alarms are inactive the control panel shall display an inactive auditory alarm symbol from Table D.201 Graphical symbols for ALARM SYSTEMS of standard IEC 60601-1-8.
If the same alert-stop-start sequence occurs 3 or more times in ten minutes, infusion will be stopped, and an audible alarm sounded.
The Control Panel confirms operation after power-on self-test of sound of audible alarm,
The Control Panel confirms operation after power-on self-test of display of visual information, and
The Control Panel confirms operation after power-on self-test of tactile response (button press).
The PCA pump shall resume prescribed infusion when the Start button is pressed.
The PCA pump shall display infusion rate currently pumping.
A clinician must personally confirm the prescription is for the patient to be infused.
Prescriptions that violate a hard limit of the drug in the drug library shall be rejected with visible and audible indication when confirmation is attempted by the clinician.
Prescriptions that violate the soft limits of the drug in the drug library shall issue a visible and audible warning requiring a soft limit confirmation by the clinician.
The basal flow rate, Fbasal, is prescribed by a physician, and entered into the PCA pump by scanning the prescription from the drug container label as it is loaded into the reservoir.

The pump shall maintain a minimum KVO flow rate of FKV O = 1 ml/hr at all times during infusion, even during alarms, unless the alarm also stops flow, or the stop button is pressed. Table 4 defines which alarms also stop drug flow completely.
A patient-requested bolus shall be delivered at its prescribed rate, Fbolus, in addition to the prescribed basal flow rate, Fbasal, but no more than the maximum flow rate for the pump, Fmax.
Any alarm stops basal rate delivery either halting pump or switching to KVO rate as defined in Table 4.
Any alarm stops patient-requested bolus delivery either halting pump or switching to KVO rate as defined in Table 4.

Patient-requested bolus shall not be delivered if infusing prescribed V T BI will exceed hard limits retrieved from the drug library for the volume of drug infused over a period of time. Pump rate shall be reduced to KVO and a max dose warning be issued.
The mechanical pump shall halt pumping when commanded, or caused in response to an alarm condition.
Upon the clinician’s pressing of the start button, start infusion prescribed.
Upon the clinician’s pressing of the stop button, stop infusion.
Before infusion, the door must be closed and locked. (UC1.10 §4.1.1)
Prescribed V T BI and rate shall not exceed the maximum VTBI limit set by the drug library from the hospital pharmacy for the drug loaded in the PCA pump.
The PCA pump shall use a physician’s prescription as device parameters.
Prescriptions that violate a hard limit of the drug in the drug library shall be rejected with visible and audible indication when confirmation is attempted by the clinician.
A clinician must personally confirm the prescription is for the patient to be infused.
Prescriptions that violate the soft limits of the drug in the drug library shall issue a visible and audible warning requiring a soft limit confirmation by the clinician.
The patient’s prescription shall be retained for at least.∆ data = 96 hours after the PCA pump is turned-off and unplugged.
A clinician must personally confirm the prescription is for the patient to be infused.
Prescriptions that violate a hard limit of the drug in the drug library shall be rejected with visible and audible indication when confirmation is attempted by the clinician.
Prescriptions that violate the soft limits of the drug in the drug library shall issue a visible and audible warning requiring a soft limit confirmation by the clinician.
The ICE Interface shall transmit current operating status and infusion rate to the ICE system.
The ICE interface shall transmit events, alarms, and warnings to the ICE system.
The ICE interface shall allow a clinician to set the duration of clinician-requested boluses through an ICE supervisor user interface.
The PCA pump shall switch to KVO infusion rate when commanded through its ICE interface.
The PCA pump shall resume prescribed infusion when commanded through its ICE interface.
When the PCA pump is not connected to an ICE network, or the ICE network connection fails, the PCA pump shall operate as a singular, stand-alone device.
The ICE interface may inactivate alarms.
Clinicians authorization to operate the PCA pump must be authenticated. (UC1.4 §4.1.1)
Patient’s identity and admittance to the hospital must be authenticated. (UC1.6 §4.1.1)
Drug container must have a valid prescription for the particular patient to be infused by the PCA pump.
Drug library information shall be authenticated before it is accepted.

Patient-requested bolus shall not be delivered if infusing prescribed V T BI will exceed hard limits retrieved from the drug library for the volume of drug infused over a period of time. Pump rate shall be reduced to KVO and a max dose warning be issued.
Patient-requested bolus shall not be delivered more often than a prescribed minimum time between patient-requested bolus, ∆prb.
The drug loaded into the reservoir must also be found in the PCA pump’s drug in library.
The PCA pump shall maintain an electronic event log to record each action taken by the pump and each event sensed of its environment.
Each log entry shall have a time stamp with its time of occurrence.
Information in event and Fault Logs shall be retained for at least ∆ log = 1000 hours after the PCA pump is turned-off and unplugged.
The event log shall record 30 days of typical events before overwriting oldest event records first.
A patient-requested bolus shall be delivered at its prescribed rate, Fbolus, in addition to the prescribed basal flow rate, Fbasal, but no more than the maximum flow rate for the pump, Fmax.
The basal flow rate, Fbasal, is prescribed by a physician, and entered into the PCA pump by scanning the prescription from the drug container label as it is loaded into the reservoir.
The PCA pump shall use a physician’s prescription as device parameters.
Prior to, or coincident with, loading the drug reservoir must also enter prescription on the drug container’s label using the scanner.
The scanner shall read and authenticate information from the patient’s wristband.
The scanner shall read and authenticate information from the clinician’s badge.
The scanner shall read and authenticate information from the drug’s package label.
Clinicians authorization to operate the PCA pump must be authenticated. (UC1.4 §4.1.1)
Patient’s identity and admittance to the hospital must be authenticated. (UC1.6 §4.1.1)
Drug container must have a valid prescription for the particular patient to be infused by the PCA pump.
Drug library information shall be authenticated before it is accepted.
Patient information must be restricted to those providing care for the patient, and the patient.
Provisioning (or re-provisioning) shall not be possible through an ICE network.
Provisioning shall be a single, unitary block-transfer.
All materials that contact fluid shall be biocompatible.
The pump shall be able to deliver basal infusion at flows throughout the basal infusion flow range of Fbasal min = 1 to Fbasal max = 10 ml/hr.
The pump shall deliver basal infusion at the prescribed basal rate within a basal infusion flow tolerance of Fbasal tol = 0.5 ml/hr of the prescribed basal rate.
The mechanical pump shall pump drug at prescribed flow rates for basal, bolus, and KVO infusion when commanded.
The mechanical pump shall halt pumping when commanded, or caused in response to an alarm condition.
When the stop button is pressed, the current pump stroke shall be completed prior to stopping the pump.
During normal use and/or single fault condition of the equipment, continuous reverse delivery shall not be possible.
When an occlusion alarm occurs, the pump shall be stopped immediately without completing the current pump stroke.
The mechanical pump shall not allow reverse flow from the patient into the pump.
The PCA pump shall measure drug flow within a tolerance of Fmd f tol = 0 .1 ml/hr.
The PCA pump shall detect upstream occlusion.
The PCA pump shall measure drug flow within a tolerance of Fmd f tol = 0 .1 ml/hr.
The PCA pump shall detect downstream occlusion.
The PCA pump shall detect air-in-line embolism (bubble).
The drug reservoir holds liquid pain-killer supplied by the hospital pharmacy and loaded into the PCA pump by the clinician.
The drug reservoir shall measure its contents.
The measured drug volume shall be within Vrt = 1 ml of the actual drug volume.
When an empty-reservoir alarm occurs, the current pump stroke shall be completed prior to stopping the pump.

Because the drugs used for analgesia are often narcotic, requiring Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) tracking if used in the United States, the drug reservoir and means to change prescriptions during infusion must be inhibited with a locked, tamper-resistant door.
Hospital procedures must endow the attending clinician access to the door key, yet prevent other persons’ access.
The PCA pump case must be at least difficult to breech as its tamper-resistant door. Breaking the case shall not be easier to access the drug reservoir than breeching the door.
An open door alarm shall be triggered when the reservoir door is opened while the pump is not stopped.
The PCA pump shall implement a safety architecture that separates normal operation from fault detection and response.
Hardware faults that prevent operation of the Control Panel shall illuminate a hardware fault indicator (light-emitting diode). (EC22f §4.2.22)
The PCA pump shallissue alarms and warnings that require clinician attention.

If delivered basal flow rate exceeds the prescribed basal rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue an basal over-infusion alarm (EC7 §4.2.7).

If delivered basal flow rate is less than the prescribed basal rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue an basal under-infusion warning (EC4.2.8).

If delivered patient-requested bolus flow rate exceeds the prescribed patient-requested bolus rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 1 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue a bolus over-infusion alarm (EC4.2.7).

If delivered patient-requested bolus flow rate is less than the prescribed bolus rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 1 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue a bolus under-infusion warning (EC4.2.8).

If delivered clinician-requested bolus flow rate exceeds the calculated square bolus rate by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue a square bolus over-infusion alarm (EC4.2.7).
Prescriptions that violate a hard limit of the drug in the drug library shall be rejected with visible and audible indication when confirmation is attempted by the clinician.
Prescriptions that violate the soft limits of the drug in the drug library shall issue a visible and audible warning requiring a soft limit confirmation by the clinician.
An air-in-line alarm shall be triggered by the pump if detectable air bubbles are infused into the patient.
An upstream occlusion alarm shall be triggered when the pump senses an upstream (drug reservoir side) occlusion exceeding Puo = 1 psi.
A downstream occlusion alarm shall be triggered if the pump senses a downstream (patient side) occlusion exceeding Pdo = 10 psi.
When an occlusion alarm occurs, the pump shall be stopped immediately without completing the current pump stroke.
When an empty-reservoir alarm occurs, the current pump stroke shall be completed prior to stopping the pump.

If delivered basal flow rate exceeds the prescribed basal rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue an basal over-infusion alarm (EC7 §4.2.7).

If delivered basal flow rate is less than the prescribed basal rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue an basal under-infusion warning (EC4.2.8).

If delivered patient-requested bolus flow rate exceeds the prescribed patient-requested bolus rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 1 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue a bolus over-infusion alarm (EC4.2.7).

If delivered patient-requested bolus flow rate is less than the prescribed bolus rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 1 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue a bolus under-infusion warning (EC4.2.8).

If delivered clinician-requested bolus flow rate exceeds the calculated square bolus rate by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue a square bolus over-infusion alarm (EC4.2.7).

The PCA pump shall perform a power-on self-test (POST) to assure system integrity after being turned on, yet before any infusion begins. Failure of POST shall raise a POST alarm , stop pump, record it in the Fault Log, and display the reason for failure on the user interface. (EC4 §4.2.4)

The PCA pump shall perform periodic self-tests to assure system integrity during long periods of use. Failure of a self-test shall raise a self-test alarm , stop pump, record it in the Fault Log, and display the reason for failure on the user interface. (EC22c §4.2.22)
The PCA pump shall have continuous fault-detection and masking. Hardware monitors of thread heartbeat, memory error correction codes are examples. (EC22d §4.2.22)
Occurrence of unavoidable single-event upsets caused by cosmic-ray-induced high- and thermal-energy neutrons must be either masked, or detected to fail-stop. (EC22d §4.2.22)
The PCA pump shall maintain an electronic fault log to record each fault condition, and the associated alarm and/or alert issued.
Each log entry shall have a time stamp with its time of occurrence.
Information in event and Fault Logs shall be retained for at least ∆ log = 1000 hours after the PCA pump is turned-off and unplugged.
Successfully masked faults shall be recorded in the Fault Log, but not raise an alarm. (EC22e §4.2.22)
All unmasked hardware detected faults shall raise a fault alarm, stop pump, record it in the Fault Log, and display the reason for fault on the user interface. (EC22 §4.2.22)
The fault log shall record at least 1000 faults before overwriting oldest fault records first.
A real-time clock must produce timestamps accurate to 10 ms.
